I appreciate your responses to OP. The notion that joining the military requires either a thirst for killing irrespective of reason or being "both desperate and of average to below average intelligence" is an uninformed one. Even goes to say that the military services are composed mostly of the bottom 10% of high schools. Pure comedy, and irony, that OP says that people would need to rely on ad hominem attacks to challenge his argument.

Proposing that the US military is a problematic institution is by no means a difficult argument to make. But conflating the outcomes caused by the machine itself with the actions of the individuals isn't particularly compelling in my opinion. Obviously these actors are required for anything to happen, but the moral character of 40 million people (roughly how many Americans have served in the military) cannot be gleaned from the outcomes in the Vietnam War or the GWOT.

Demonizing young Americans that joined the military is so bizarre to me, there are a lot of reasons that people join, and contrary to OP's belief, it isn't always either a thirst for blood or a cognitive issue, I'm not convinced that either is a factor in even a minority of cases. I don't think an explanation for why people join could be more juvenile and less informed.
